clue.text: Neptune has been leaking? Hope your trip is safe!

parts.note: Neptune is the Roman sea god, so 'Neptune has' gives GOD'S, a god's
to have peed is to have leaked, in the childish sense of passing water

explanation.surface: A worried note about the sea god springing a leak, followed by a wish for a safe voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neptune has' reads as GOD'S, with the apostrophe dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is an old farewell wishing a traveller success and a safe journey.

clue.text: Pet jumps up to grab a stick

indicators.note: to grab is to hold, so the turned word holds the next piece inside it
in a down entry, jumping up means the word for the pet is written bottom to top

parts.note: a dog is the classic household pet

explanation.surface: An excited pet leaping to snatch a thrown stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumps up' turns DOG into GOD, which 'to grab' then wraps round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A goad is a pointed stick used to drive cattle forward, a prodding rod.

clue.text: With spirit lacking, heart lost at the expected time

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, and here that middle letter is dropped

parts.note: doing something dully is doing it listlessly, without spirit

explanation.surface: Someone drooping and dispirited, yet still turning up on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart lost' removes the middle L of DULLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Duly means properly or punctually, as in 'the train duly arrived', at the right moment.

clue.text: Whiteness of cloud tipped with gold

indicators.note: in a down entry the tip is the bottom end, so the gold piece is placed after the cloud

parts.note: a pall is a dark cloud hanging over something, as in a pall of smoke
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A white cloud whose edge is lit with gold, like a sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallor is an unhealthy paleness of the face, a lack of colour.

clue.text: Sealed instruction for some severe brothers

parts.note: something sealed up is enclosed, shut in
an order is an instruction or command

explanation.surface: A secret command addressed to a group of stern monks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word: the instruction is meant for the brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemplative communities such as Carthusian monks live cloistered from the world, a strict religious rule.

clue.text: Bad habits, clinging to old opinions

indicators.note: the habits cling round the abbreviation, holding it inside them

parts.note: vices are bad habits

explanation.surface: Someone whose bad habits come from holding on to outdated views.
explanation.definitionFit: Voices are expressed views, as in 'dissenting voices' at a meeting.

clue.text: Stub toes carelessly: most stupid

indicators.note: something done carelessly is jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clumsily stubbing your toes is the height of foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow-witted, so the superlative is the dullest or least perceptive.

clue.text: Example of punctuation almost unprecedented in official statement

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a comma is one punctuation mark
something unprecedented has never happened before, so it is unique

explanation.surface: A press release containing a punctuation error no one has seen before.
explanation.definitionFit: A communiqué is a formal announcement issued by a government or organisation.

clue.text: One insect, or another with small mark on, let free

indicators.note: in a down entry, being on something means sitting above it, so the small mark comes before the other insect

parts.note: a tag is a label or identifying mark
another insect: the bee

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A naturalist tagging one insect, or another, and then releasing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges LET into TLE to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The stag beetle is a large European beetle whose males have antler-like jaws.

clue.text: Refuses to play against every international team

indicators.note: against here means up against, next to, so the two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: all means every one
to black a team or firm is to boycott it, refusing to deal or play with it

explanation.surface: A side that declines to face any of its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' means up against, beside, with no order implied, so the pieces may sit either way round. New Zealand's rugby union team is named for its all-black kit.
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealand's rugby side plays test matches against other countries, so it is a national team.

clue.text: Process for making rock, a fatal day used up thinking

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word used upward is read from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: the Ides of March was the fatal day for Julius Caesar
mentation is a formal word for thinking or mental activity

explanation.surface: A grim day spent brooding about how rocks are made.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedimentary rock forms as particles settle and build up in layers over time.

clue.text: Pack round a US resort

parts.note: to tamp is to pack material firmly round something, as round a charge in a drill hole

explanation.surface: Packing a suitcase to head off to an American holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a Florida city on the Gulf coast, known for beaches and holidays.

clue.text: Leave me alone, teacher foolishly bids tutor

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: doing something foolishly jumbles it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tired academic snapping as a colleague makes a silly request of a tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase on a hotel door sign asks others not to interrupt you.

clue.text: Hawks wine round hospital showing war damage

indicators.note: the selling word goes round the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
hock is a German white wine from the Rhineland

explanation.surface: A trader peddling wine to a hospital that treats wounded soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts H inside SELLS to give SHELLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shell shock is psychological trauma from combat, a mental wound of war.

clue.text: Gained hair untidily that's on the side of the head

definitions.text: that's on the side of the head

indicators.note: untidy hair is messed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone who has grown scruffy locks over the sides of their head.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing aid is a small device worn behind or in the ear to amplify sound.

clue.text: One working in bed offers nothing for woman to embrace

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the pronoun wraps round the zero

parts.note: her is a pronoun standing for a woman
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A suggestive line about what someone in bed offers a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not a bed for sleeping in.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoer is a gardener using a hoe to weed the soil of a flower bed.

clue.text: Indulgent secretary leaves hard copy letter

indicators.note: the secretary leaves, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a hard copy is a printed paper version of a document
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A soft-hearted secretary walks out, leaving a printed letter behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes PA out of PAPER to give PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A permissive parent or regime is lenient, allowing much freedom.

clue.text: Eccentric dispute in delta region

parts.note: an eccentric is a cam, an off-centre wheel in machinery
to argue is to dispute

explanation.surface: An odd quarrel breaks out somewhere in a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an anagram signal, but here it is a noun from engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camargue is the marshy area of the Rhône delta in southern France.

clue.text: Titled lady no one associated with a lord, somehow

indicators.note: done somehow, in some unspecified way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A noblewoman with no one at her side except an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: LORNA DOONE is R D Blackmore's novel; its heroine gives the book its title and is revealed to be of noble birth.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the title character of the novel, and is in fact a lady by birth.

clue.text: Out loud, not many will be encouraging

indicators.note: what follows is said aloud, and the spoken words match another word's sound

parts.note: not many is few, so 'few will' shortens to few'll

explanation.surface: A gloomy prediction that hardly anyone will speak up in support.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuel a feeling or trend is to feed it and stimulate it further.

clue.text: Playwright's agreed a firm rise

indicators.note: in a down entry, a rise means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: yes is the word for agreeing
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A dramatist has agreed to a pay rise from a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reverses YESACO into OCASEY; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean O'Casey was an Irish dramatist, author of Juno and the Paycock.

clue.text: Run taken from excellent ball by youngster? That's routine

indicators.note: by means beside, so the youngster stands next to the rest

parts.note: a son is a young boy

indicators.note: the run is removed from the excellent word

parts.note: grand means excellent
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A boy leaves a splendid ball early, and it seems this is habitual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' removes R from GRAND to give GAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A song and dance is an elaborate fuss or a stage act, a performance routine.

clue.text: King's imprimatur lends organisation at first a certain weight

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of these four words is used

explanation.surface: A royal seal of approval brings structure and authority to an undertaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilo is a kilogram, a fixed unit of mass equal to a thousand grams.

clue.text: Like hens, eat a quantity of grain

definitions.meaning: to eat as hens do, striking at food with the beak
an old dry measure for grain, a quarter of a bushel

explanation.surface: Chickens feeding on scattered grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the farmyard: the birds' feeding action and an old dry measure.

clue.text: Asian native suggesting his phone was silent?

parts.note: silent here stands for nothing, as in nothing was heard, and nothing is the zero shape
a phone that sounds has rung, so the past tense of ring stands in for the phone's action

explanation.surface: An animal whose name seems to say no call came in.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces combine as 'nothing rang', which is what happened when the phone was silent; the question mark flags that loose, playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape found only in the rainforests of Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Limit on height of church is to stimulate new ideas

indicators.note: on means next to, so the limit is placed alongside the church's top

parts.note: to rein in is to limit, and a rein is a restraint
a spire is the tall pointed top of a church

explanation.surface: A cap on church spire heights is meant to spark fresh thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinspire someone is to inspire them again, rekindling creativity.

clue.text: Vital to carry card with name to donate this?

indicators.note: the vital word carries the others inside it

parts.note: key means vital or essential

indicators.note: with joins the card and the name side by side

parts.note: an ID is an identity card

explanation.surface: It is vital to carry a donor card with your name on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue evokes an organ donor card, and the definition leans on that picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidneys are the organs most often given by living and deceased donors.

clue.text: O boy! Mink's fantastic for me

indicators.note: something fantastic is wild and fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An excited exclamation over a mink coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Mink is 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In my book is an idiom meaning in my opinion, as far as I am concerned.
